cause_quote: The diff set update-mode work policy to `(params.timeoutMs ?? null)` and replaced the npm child's `timeoutMs: Math.max(timeoutMs, 300_000)` with `timeoutMs: resolveInstallWorkTimeoutMs(workTimeoutMs, Math.max(timeoutMs, 300_000))`, making the forwarded internal allowance override the five-minute minimum.
user_saw: A healthy plugin update could time out after the core upgrade even when the operator supplied no timeout.
summary: The fix carries the operator's explicit timeout separately from internal allowances so post-core plugin work can finish while metadata probes stay bounded.
reasoning: I checked the causing commit's parent and confirmed that the existing post-core updater already forwarded its numeric allowance to the npm installer, where a five-minute minimum let the reported 65-second child finish. PR #153043 made the same forwarded number a work deadline, so the 60-second allowance in the reported reproduction stopped the child.
